newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK reversion to help China financial mkts - HK Exch.
newsitem.headline: HK reversion to help China financial mkts - HK Exch.

text.p: China had a unique short cut to help it overcome problems encountered in the development of its domestic financial markets when it inherits Hong Kong next year, the chairman of the Stock Exchange of Hong Kong said on Friday.
"China does, by an accident of history, have a relatively mature market at its disposal, in the form of Hong Kong," Edgar Cheng told a symposium.
Cheng said the problems China faced in opening up its domestic markets were inevitable hiccups.
"It is unsurprising that they have had some of the same problems as markets elsewhere in their early stages of development," he said.

Cheng said he believed there was a unique opportunity to link China's development and financing needs to Hong Kong, its own mature international financial centre, and thus to take a short cut to overcoming some of these problems.
The British colony will return to Chinese rule in mid-1997.
It was unprecedented that a developed international financial centre with a sophisticated market infrastructure should be grafted onto the economy of a developing nation, Cheng said.
"It will be surprising if the process does not create some stresses and strains," he said. "But the potential rewards for both China and Hong Kong are great indeed."
